past_medical_history: Parkinson's disease (diagnosed 6 years ago, on levodopa/carbidopa)

social_history.recent_stressor: Husband diagnosed with terminal lung cancer 3 months ago — caregiver burden; anticipatory grief; change in role from patient to caregiver

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert. Tearful when discussing husband. Cognitive testing: MoCA 26/30 (mild impairment consistent with PD-MCI baseline).
neurological_exam.motor: BASELINE PD: mild right-predominant bradykinesia and cogwheel rigidity (4 Hz rest tremor, right hand). NEW: LEFT hand now shows NEW tremor at 8-10 Hz, active and action tremor, suppressed with distraction, entrains to examiner-imposed rhythm — these features are INCONSISTENT with PD tremor (PD tremor is 4-6 Hz, rest-predominant, does NOT entrain to external rhythm). NEW left arm weakness 3/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Normal 2+ symmetric. No Babinski. PD patients do not have pathological reflexes typically.
neurological_exam.coordination: Mild right finger-nose imprecision (PD baseline). Left arm: NEW apparent ataxia — inconsistent; resolves with attention.
neurological_exam.gait: Baseline PD gait (mild right-sided Parkinsonian shuffle, reduced right arm swing). New: left leg dragging added — INCONSISTENT with Parkinson progression (PD is asymmetric early, eventual bilateral but from the involved side).
neurological_exam.additional: DIAGNOSTIC PUZZLE: Parkinson's disease patient with new symptoms on the CONTRALATERAL side. In PD, progression typically involves worsening on the AFFECTED side (right) first, then slow bilateral spread. New prominent LEFT side symptoms appearing acutely in a known PD patient with identified psychosocial stressor is highly suspicious for FND superimposed on PD.

patient.chief_complaint: New left-sided tremor and weakness — developed over 4 weeks
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Q is a 61-year-old retired accountant with established Parkinson's disease (right-sided onset, on levodopa/carbidopa and pramipexole, stable for 2 years) who presents with 4-week history of new left-sided tremor and left arm weakness. Her known PD has been right-predominant since diagnosis 6 years ago with satisfactory response to medications. The new left-sided symptoms developed over 4 weeks, approximately 1 month after her husband was diagnosed with terminal lung cancer. She is now providing full care for her husband while managing her own PD. The clinical question is whether the new symptoms represent PD progression to the left side (which occurs in PD over time) or a new process. The NEW LEFT tremor has specific features on examination that distinguish it from her known right-sided PD tremor: it is higher frequency (8-10 Hz vs 4 Hz for PD), suppressed by distracting tasks, action-predominant rather than rest-predominant, and entrains to examiner-imposed rhythms — ALL of these features are inconsistent with PD tremor. Additionally, the acute onset (4 weeks) of prominent contralateral involvement coinciding with a major life stressor is atypical for PD progression.

additional_observations: Normal brain MRI — no new structural lesion
mri.impression: Normal brain MRI without new structural lesion. No new lesion explaining acute left-sided symptoms. Stable findings. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.description: Normal symmetric background with mild posterior alpha slowing to 8 Hz (consistent with PD-associated cognitive changes).

eeg.impression: No new epileptiform activity. No focal changes. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Markedly reduced right striatal uptake — RIGHT putamen severely reduced (consistent with 6-year right-predominant PD)
MILDLY reduced left striatal uptake — LEFT putamen 1.6 binding ratio (borderline reduced; normal >2.0)

quantitative_data.interpretation: Asymmetric DaTscan: markedly reduced right, mildly reduced left — consistent with known right-predominant PD with mild early left involvement. HOWEVER: the mild left reduction alone CANNOT explain the 8-10 Hz high-frequency action tremor and acute 4-week weakness — mild DaTscan abnormality does not correlate with sudden severe left symptoms.

output.impression: Abnormal — bilateral reduced striatal dopamine transporter uptake, right greater than left. Right putamen markedly reduced. Left putamen borderline reduced (binding ratio 1.6; normal >2.0). Findings are consistent with a presynaptic dopaminergic deficit. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: FND superimposed on early contralateral PD progression. The mild left DaTscan change is PD; the acute clinical presentation is FND.

findings.finding: RIGHT HAND tremor: 4.2 Hz, rest-predominant, not suppressible with voluntary movement — consistent with Parkinsonian tremor. Fixed frequency.

LEFT HAND tremor: 8-9 Hz VARIABLE frequency, action-predominant, ENTRAINS to examiner-imposed frequency (measured via accelerometer — when examiner vibrates arm at 3 Hz, left hand tremor changes to 3 Hz). Variability and entrainment confirm functional tremor.

output.impression: Right hand: rhythmic tremor at 4.2 Hz with stable frequency, consistent with rest tremor of extrapyramidal origin. Left hand: variable-frequency tremor with frequency entrainment to voluntary contralateral movements and amplitude reduction on distraction, consistent with features of functional tremor. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: Right: continue levodopa for organic PD tremor. Left: FND treatment for functional tremor.

Right-sided PD symptoms should be assessed for adequate levodopa dosing
Consider dopaminergic augmentation if right PD symptoms worsening — but FND symptoms will not improve with levodopa

results.title: FND in caregivers: stress and grief as precipitants

output.summary: Caregiver stress and anticipatory grief are recognised precipitants of functional neurological disorder in patients who simultaneously manage a chronic neurological condition of their own. Published literature documents that the dual patient-caregiver role creates psychosocial vulnerability associated with symptom exacerbation. Psychosocial support services and respite care have been described in case series as adjuncts to FND-specific multidisciplinary treatment. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Functional neurological disorder — functional left tremor and left arm weakness superimposed on established right-predominant Parkinson's disease (mixed organic PD + FND)

differential.likelihood: Partial — mild left DaTscan reduction confirms early left PD progression, but this ALONE cannot explain the acute 8-10 Hz high-frequency tremor with entrainment and 3/5 arm weakness
differential.key_features: Mild left DaTscan reduction confirms early contralateral PD progression but is disproportionate to the acute 8-10 Hz high-frequency action tremor with entrainment; PD tremor is 4-6 Hz rest-predominant and does not entrain to external rhythms
Pramipexole is a dopamine agonist (not an antagonist) — it does not cause drug-induced parkinsonism; dopamine antagonists (metoclopramide, antipsychotics) cause drug-induced parkinsonism
No autonomic failure (no orthostatic hypotension), good levodopa response, no cerebellar signs, DaTscan asymmetric (MSA has more symmetric DaTscan); MRI normal

Essential tremor is bilateral symmetric, action-predominant, 6-12 Hz — but it does NOT entrain to externally imposed rhythm; accelerometry shows variable frequency and entrainment confirming functional tremor

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain — exclude new structural lesion in PD patient
DaTscan — assess bilateral dopaminergic deficit; correlate with clinical presentation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Right markedly reduced (PD); left mildly reduced (early contralateral PD) but insufficient to explain acute severe left tremor

optimal_actions.action: Tremor accelerometry — distinguish PD tremor from functional tremor by frequency analysis and entrainment
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Right: 4 Hz fixed PD tremor (organic); Left: 8-9 Hz variable with entrainment (functional)

optimal_actions.action: Labs — exclude thyrotoxicosis, Wilson's (metabolic tremor causes)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal TSH, ceruloplasmin — metabolic tremor excluded

optimal_actions.action: Psychiatric evaluation — anticipatory grief and caregiver burden as precipitants
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Moderately severe depression; high caregiver burden

critical_actions: DaTscan — bilateral assessment to correlate organic left PD progression with functional overlay
Tremor accelerometry — frequency and entrainment distinguish PD from functional tremor
FND treatment for left side; continue levodopa for right PD symptoms
Palliative care referral for husband (indirect but critical treatment component)
contraindicated_actions: Increasing levodopa/pramipexole for functional left tremor — dopaminergic medications do not treat FND and adding dose increases risk
Attributing all symptoms to PD without distinguishing organic from functional component
key_reasoning_points: Parkinson's tremor is 4-6 Hz, REST-predominant, and does NOT entrain to external rhythms — tremor that entrains is functional
DaTscan shows only MILD left reduction — disproportionate to acute severe clinical left symptoms; mild DaTscan abnormality confirms early PD progression but cannot explain acute 8-10 Hz action tremor
Mixed PD + FND is a recognized entity — FND has higher prevalence in patients with existing neurological disease; positive functional signs distinguish the functional component from the organic
The critical teaching: increasing levodopa to treat functional tremor is ineffective and exposes patient to dopaminergic side effects

red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute all left-sided symptoms to PD progression and increase dopaminergic medications
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild left DaTscan reduction represents early contralateral PD progression (expected over 6 years) but is disproportionate to the acute severe functional left tremor; accelerometry confirms functional tremor characteristics

metadata.notes: Diagnostic puzzle FND — functional left tremor superimposed on right-predominant PD. DaTscan mildly reduced left (early PD) but disproportionate to acute severe functional tremor. Accelerometry is key.
